title: Behind the White House's UFO Silence — Liberation Times
excerpt: Throughout the summer, rumours swirled that President Donald Trump was preparing an extraordinary announcement.
content:
Written by Christopher Sharp - 17 November 2026

Throughout the summer, rumours swirled that President Donald Trump was preparing an extraordinary announcement.

He would tell Americans, and the world, that we are not alone in the universe.

Several sources urged Liberation Times to take the prospect seriously. Sources familiar with the President’s inner circle and members of his family expressed alarm and confidence that he could deliver disclosure.

That announcement has yet to come.

Liberation Times is aware of contact between White House staff and advocates for transparency on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP). Some discussions stretched late into the night, discussing navigation of alleged UAP programs involving non-human lifeforms.

Alongside those conversations, a formal advisory structure took shape.

In June, an official from the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) described the arrangements to Liberation Times. The official said ODNI had established a UAP Governance Board alongside the FBI and Department of War (DoW).

Its charter includes coordinating investigations, improving data collection and supporting declassification.

Harvard astrophysicist Avi Loeb publicly announced one of its supporting groups. In a 13 June article, he described assembling the UAP Science Advisory Council. Loeb said government agencies had tasked him with bringing together scientists to help investigate the phenomenon.

Other organisations also joined discussions at ODNI. They included the Disclosure Foundation, a nonprofit advocating UAP transparency, and To The Stars, a media company involved in UAP research.

Aaron Lukas, the Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence, publicly identified their involvement on 17 September. He thanked both organisations and Loeb’s council for participating as advisers to the Governance Board.

However, other advisory councils working alongside ODNI, the FBI and DoW remain undisclosed.

Questions about ODNI’s role also extend to an alleged operation to attract UAP. As Liberation Times previously reported, released government records describe a senior intelligence official witnessing glowing orbs at a sensitive U.S. testing facility.

Jordan Flowers, executive director of the Disclosure Foundation, an advocacy group campaigning for UAP transparency, has alleged that these encounters formed part of a successful ODNI luring operation, although the released records do not explicitly confirm that purpose.

He promised to investigate immediately following the interview.

Liberation Times subsequently asked whether he had followed through. A White House spokesperson replied:

‘Refer you to the President’s comments.’

The response left unanswered whether Trump had indeed investigated.

In the interview, when pushed on whether he was interested in the topic because other people were, Trump said:

“I would like to find out whether or not it's true. I will tell you, you have a lot of very solid people that believe it's true.”

The interview came amid extensive discussion of the allegations involving such programs by people in his orbit.

Fox News host Sean Hannity, a longtime Trump ally, interviewed former U.S. Air Force intelligence specialist Dylan Borland - a UAP whistleblower - and former FBI agent Ben Hansen. Their conversation covered alleged recovered craft and government secrecy. Hannity said he would raise the issue with the President when he next saw him.

Television psychologist Phil McGraw, better known as Dr Phil, interviewed former Air Force intelligence officer and UAP whistleblower David Grusch. They discussed Grusch’s allegations of secret retrieval efforts involving non-human craft and their occupants.

There are also accounts of information reaching Trump during his first term.

Former Pentagon official Luis Elizondo described one such route in his 2024 memoir, Imminent. He wrote that Jay Stratton, who led the government’s UAP Task Force, briefed National Security Council members. According to Elizondo, those officials subsequently briefed Trump.

The President’s son, Donald Trump Jr., has also interviewed Elizondo three times on his Triggered podcast. Their discussions have covered UAP and alleged secret government programs.

Republican Congressman Eric Burlison also recounted an alleged briefing given directly to Trump, attributing the account to David Grusch, who previously served as a special adviser on Burlison’s staff.

He said, according to what he was told, Trump had been briefed on alleged human-alien hybrids during his first term, adding that the briefing took place while Trump was facing impeachment proceedings.

“He had like this existential briefing that just kind of rocked his worldview,” Burlison said.

Burlison added that he had been told Trump joked that then-Congressman Adam Schiff ‘must be one of them’, referring to the alleged hybrid beings.

Liberation Times also understands that Trump’s new Chief of Staff is very aware of alleged UAP programs. 

The White House named Stephen Miller Chief of Staff on 6 November, following Republican losses in the midterm elections.

Miller previously served as Trump’s deputy chief of staff.

In August, Secretary of State Marco Rubio indicated that Miller was overseeing the UAP portfolio. Sources told Liberation Times that his work included investigating alleged hidden programs to retrieve and reverse-engineer non-human craft.

Congress member and UAP transparency advocate, Tim Burchett recently told Cabot Phillips that Stephen Miller had told him:

"There's some people that are in government that I feel like are very bad people that don't want us to have this information for whatever reason.”

Miller’s promotion has left uncertainty over who now leads that work.

Republican Congressman Eric Burlison, a member of the congressional UAP Caucus, voiced similar concerns during a 10 November interview. Speaking to journalist Matt Laslo for Ask a Pol UAP, he said Trump had taken Miller off the UAP topic.

Burlison questioned whether Miller would retain time for it. He also said he did not know whether anyone would replace him. 

The uncertainty comes as Congress considers another route to disclosure.

On 22 July, the House adopted Burlison’s UAP Disclosure Act as an amendment to the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act. The proposal would establish an independent records review board and extend disclosure requirements to covered government contractors.

Its fate in the final defence bill remains unresolved.

Meanwhile, the administration has continued releasing records through its Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters, or PURSUE. The Department of War announced the initiative’s first release on 8 May.

The releases have not clarified what the White House has learned about the origins of UAP or the intentions of any entities behind them, nor how much the administration intends to disclose.

Democrats will take control of both chambers of Congress in January 2027, when the 120th Congress begins. Their commitment to UAP transparency will face a test after Republican-led hearings and investigations championed by Representatives Anna Paulina Luna, Tim Burchett and Eric Burlison, including through Luna’s declassification task force. 

Speaking about the current situation within Washington D.C., Jordan Flowers, executive director of the Disclosure Foundation, told Liberation Times:

“The next several weeks are a test of whether Congress can lock in real progress before leadership changes on January 3, through another hearing and the full UAP Disclosure Act in the NDAA, and whether the new majority will build on that work with a select committee that has subpoena power.

“At the White House, the public messaging has been inconsistent, but the PURSUE releases show continued interest, and our job is to keep this a bipartisan issue anchored in national security and accountability for waste, fraud, and abuse.”

Democratic Representative André Carson, who chaired the first public congressional UAP hearing in more than 50 years in May 2022, is reportedly pushing for a dedicated UAP select committee.

Carson, whose seat on the House Intelligence Committee gives him a direct role in overseeing U.S. intelligence agencies and their classified activities, previously discussed the idea with journalist Matt Laslo in 2025. 

Commenting on that possibility, Flowers told Liberation Times:

“In the 120th Congress, a select committee on UAP led by Representative André Carson would be wonderful progress: it would not face the six-month renewal question that has hung over the current task force, and it would have subpoena power from day one.

“Representative Carson’s experience on both Intelligence and Oversight would also make him well placed to connect the two committees that matter most on this topic, and we hope any new structure stays bipartisan and builds on the work Republican members have already done.”

Any potential disclosure could expose intelligence capabilities that extend well beyond UAP.

Sources previously told Liberation Times that the CIA’s Weapons and Counterproliferation Mission Center (WCPMC) has helped assess the phenomenon’s potential non-human origins. They described work to identify the different intelligences that might control these objects and assess their intentions.

According to those sources, WCPMC drew on intelligence collected across the U.S. government. This included space-based collection by the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO), which develops and operates reconnaissance satellites.

They also identified the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA), National Security Agency (NSA) and National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) as contributors.

The sources described inputs spanning signals intelligence, measurement and signature intelligence, and geospatial intelligence. They said WCPMC collected and analysed UAP information from the atmosphere, space and undersea environments.

The CIA publicly confirms WCPMC’s existence. It describes its mission centres as combining operational, analytical and technical capabilities to address national security threats. 

An intelligence-community source told Liberation Times that detailed technical assessments of UAP from the WCPMC were shared among specialists across intelligence agencies. Finished assessments were then prepared for senior policymakers.

Such intelligence work, alongside the recovery and reverse-engineering of foreign technology, serves U.S. national security.

Some of the capabilities involved may remain classified even if the administration chooses to acknowledge any possible non-human presence.

One potential route to disclosure is the separate UAP effort allegedly operating under White House oversight.

If reports of luring and shootdown operations are accurate, that effort could give the administration evidence obtained independently of existing programs.

It might provide a path to disclosure while protecting sensitive intelligence sources and methods.

Whether that effort has produced such evidence, and whether Trump intends to release it, remains unclear.
